requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1 (active on running kernel)
requirements.summary: After a real reboot (boot_id changed from b1181481... to 83f0baed...), /proc/cmdline shows audit=1 and dmesg confirms 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' with audit_enabled=1 and no failure messages.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (on-disk boot configuration retains audit=1)
requirements.summary: audit=1 was added to default_kernel_opts in /etc/update-extlinux.conf and update-extlinux regenerated /boot/extlinux.conf with APPEND ... audit=1 before the reboot; after the reboot both files still contain audit=1, and the running kernel reflects it, demonstrating actual persistence rather than a one-time boot flag.

overall_summary: The executor correctly added audit=1 to /etc/update-extlinux.conf's default_kernel_opts, regenerated /boot/extlinux.conf via update-extlinux, and directly verified the change across an actual reboot: pre-reboot baseline boot_id/uptime were captured, the reboot was acknowledged and produced a genuinely different post-reboot boot_id, and post-reboot evidence shows /proc/cmdline containing audit=1, dmesg confirming the audit subsystem initialized successfully, and both the source config and generated bootloader config still containing audit=1. This constitutes a complete before/disruption/after evidence chain directly demonstrating the required persistent boot behavior.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; multiple reboots were not tested, though one full cycle with config re-verification is sufficient to demonstrate persistence for this task.
A small residual file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the reboot trigger command was left on node1; it is inert and does not affect functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were purposeful: editing /etc/update-extlinux.conf and regenerating /boot/extlinux.conf were required to satisfy the task, and the reboot was a necessary, bounded action to verify persistence. One minor unnecessary residue: the backgrounded reboot command (cmd-04455508c3e440c8) redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log, which was not cleaned up and appears in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot as an added entry. This is low-risk, bounded log residue with no functional or security impact, but it was left in place rather than removed.
